name: runtime.send
description: Send one event to a live statechart actor (design/statecharts.md section 10) by its path as listed by runtime.statecharts or machine.actors(). Delivered in the task phase through the actor's normal send path: schema validation, strict mode and reserved-prefix rejection apply, and the input is labeled origin dev in inspection records and the statechart recording, so ouroctl replay reproduces sessions driven this way. Returns {actor, accepted, reason, states, status, changed (context keys), changes (their new values), sequence, commit, time_ms, guards}. With wait = {states?, timeout_ms?} (default 5000) it then waits, through machine.wait_for, until one of states matches (or the next commit when states is omitted) and adds wait = {matched, error}. Unknown actors and invalid events are tool errors with codes such as UnknownActor, UnknownEvent and InvalidEvent. Component machines are addressed by their exact path '<chart id>@<instance path>' (for example collapsible@panel/details; a second live instance on the same path gets #2); spawned children are 'parent/child'.

name: runtime.statecharts
description: Read ouro.machine inspection records (design/statecharts.md section 10). The first call attaches an observer to the active source generation and seeds actors from each live actor's graph and current snapshot (machine.actors(), snapshot(), chart:graph()); every call renews it, and it detaches keep_alive_ms (default 30000) after the last call, so idle instances build no records. Returns entries {sequence, time_ms, record} oldest first with sequence greater than after; time_ms is host monotonic time since launch. actors (always included when after is 0) holds each live actor's started record (with its graph) and latest record, keyed by actor path, so root actors carried across reload stay visible; seed changes whenever actors was rebuilt (attach, reload, idle reattach); pass the last seen seed to receive actors exactly when it changed. dropped is true when the bounded ring evicted records after the cursor. Poll again with after set to next. text returns each record as a JSON string, for clients with per-reply value limits such as ouro.mcp. actor = path adds actor = {actor, machine, parent, graph, snapshot}: that actor's complete current state read now, where snapshot carries the configuration (states), status (actor:status(): created for a component actor mounted but not yet started, active, done, stopped), full context, children, output, pending timers and invokes (with start times) and the currently accepted events. Together with actors this is a complete late-attach read; no history is needed. rollup = true adds rollup = {observed_since_ms, actors: [{actor, machine, parent, status, states (active leaf states), timers, invokes (pending counts), records, rejected, errors, last_error {message, time_ms}, last_event, last_time_ms, changed_ms, time_ms}]}: the system overview, where the counters cover the time since the observer attached. Instead of polling, subscribe with subscriptions/listen {notifications: {resourceSubscriptions: ["ouro://statecharts"]}} (advertised as capabilities.resources.subscribe by server/discover): the endpoint sends notifications/resources/updated when records arrive or the source reloads, at most one until the next runtime.statecharts call (reads counts calls), and nothing while idle. A live subscription keeps the observer attached like calls do.

name: runtime.inspect
description: Inspect live windows, or a window's bounded semantic tree. Use its opaque token with runtime.input or runtime.capture; inspect again after StaleDevelopmentTarget. Bounds and editor caret_bounds use logical window coordinates before clipping. Editor text_scroll reports both x and y offsets in local logical pixels. Caret geometry is reported even when hidden; masked fields omit both editor geometry properties.

name: runtime.input
description: Route one input action through the live window with a fresh inspection token. A targeted action may also pass pin, the target's inspected pin: the token may then predate later rebuilds (for example a UI that rebuilds on a timer) as long as the window and source generation are unchanged and the path still resolves to that same mounted node. A node removed and mounted again has a new pin and is rejected, even under the same keys. Click, hover, scroll, pointer_down and pointer_move require a semantic target path. For a drag, pointer_down at the source, pointer_move to the destination, then pointer_up without a target; inspect between actions. Escape cancels an internal drag. Text types printable UTF-8 into the focused field; control characters and active IME composition are rejected. Key names are tab, enter, space, escape, backspace, delete, home, end, page_up, page_down, arrow_left, arrow_right, arrow_up, arrow_down, and lowercase letters. Returns after runnable callbacks, reconciliation and backend frame submission, not display presentation or asynchronous task completion. Errors or cancellation do not undo callbacks already run.

name: runtime.capture
description: Replay a live window's current scene to a private PNG. This is software_scene_replay, not GPU readback. Requires a fresh inspection token. Returns a local path retained until four later captures or instance exit; copy it to keep it.

name: runtime.diagnostics
description: Read the active source name, source generation and latest structured reload diagnostic, plus the statechart recording {path, inputs, failed, reason} when this instance records (design/statecharts.md section 14; replay it with ouroctl replay <path> <app>). Does not evaluate Lua or change application state.

name: runtime.metrics
description: Read actual successful CPU build/layout/paint counts and timings, input-event and backend-submission counts, and retained resource counts. These are not GPU timings or input-to-presentation latency. Omit window to list all live windows.
